newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka leader orders probe into alleged murder.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka leader orders probe into alleged murder.

text.p: Sri Lankan President Chandrika Kumaratunga has ordered an inquiry into an alleged rape and killing of a Tamil woman by police in the east, her office said on Friday.
A special team of police Criminal Investigation Department detectives will be sent from Colombo to conduct the probe into the death of 37-year-old Murugesupillai Koneshwari, it said in a statement.

It quoted police as saying Koneshwari had been sleeping with her three children at home in the Central Camp area in Amparai district, 200 km (125 miles) east of Colombo, on May 17 when police and Tamil Tiger rebels exchanged gunfire.
"On the following morning, Mrs Koneshwari had been found dead with injuries which appeared to have been caused by a bomb blast," the statement said.

Subsequently, Joseph Pararajasingham, a Tamil parliamentarian from the east, complained to Kumaratunga that the woman had not been killed in the shoot-out as made out by police, but had been raped and murdered, it said.

Kumaratunga has said her government had cracked down on human rights abuses by security forces fighting Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels demanding independence for minority Tamils in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
Human rights groups have accused security forces of widespread human rights violations in the late 1980s and early 1990s but have said the situation has improved in recent years.
The government says more than 50,000 people had been killed in the war since 1983 but the rebels say the toll is higher.
